topic: automated program repair; LLM code generation; fault localization; software engineering evaluation
status: bounded candidate from one random-sampled full-text empirical study; not a novelty claim
claim: In one study of 1,431 introductory C assignments, a fault-localization/sketch/iterative-feedback pipeline repaired substantially more student programs than listed baselines/configurations, but repair success dropped to 17.1% in the hardest cyclomatic-complexity quartile under the strongest reported configuration. Access to reference code further increased repair counts while raising copying and larger-edit concerns. This supports a complexity- and task-transfer question, not a general claim that LLM-generated code is reliable or that the method works on repository-scale bugs.
positive_evidence: The sampled paper tests six approximately 7B open models and reports results across 1,431 compiling but semantically incorrect introductory C programs.

The all-model portfolio reaches 1,190/1,431 repairs (83.2%) with reference implementations under its best configuration; the strongest listed all-model portfolio without references repairs 907/1,431 (63.4%). These portfolio figures are best-of-model/configuration summaries, not a single model's expected performance.
For the hardest cyclomatic-complexity quartile, the strongest reported configuration repairs 17.1%; the authors also report that reference implementations can be copied and yield larger changes.
counterevidence: Only one of the eight sampled `ai_generated_code` papers directly evaluates LLM code repair; the other papers study classical transformations, component composition, scientific DSLs, formal specifications/foundations, a proposal, or a conceptual roadmap.
The benchmark is introductory student C assignments rather than industrial repository issues, multi-file changes, or long-term regressions.
Counterexample feedback is not uniformly beneficial across model/configuration combinations, and reference-code comparisons change both repair rate and patch size.

sources.sections: benchmark setup and tables 6/9; discussion of complexity and reference-implementation trade-off

falsifiable_test: On introductory assignments and repository-level bug-fix tasks, compare matched model/compute/test budgets with factorial ablations for fault localization, hole/sketch prompts, and counterexample feedback. Stratify by bug type and pre-repair complexity. Measure hidden-test correctness, regressions, patch size, and review effort. The candidate is weakened if gains transfer uniformly across complexity and task domains without reliability or patch-size costs. Publish per-model results, not just best-of-portfolio outcomes.
limitations: Single direct empirical study in this eight-record random sample; no independent replication, no industrial-task validation, and no field-wide literature novelty audit. Portfolio maxima should not be interpreted as one deployable system's average success rate.
